title: is done was done (passive 1)
subtitle: The office is cleaned every day.
summary: Use am/is/are or was/were with a past participle to say what happens or happened to something, without saying who does it.

lesson.heading: Somebody cleans the office
lesson.text: A cleaner comes to an office every evening with a mop and a bucket. In the morning the office is tidy again. We do not need to say who the cleaner is. We can put the office first and use the **passive**.

left.label: active
left.text: We say who does the action.

right.label: passive
right.text: The thing comes first. We do not say who does it.

lesson.heading: The form of the passive
lesson.note: The past participle of a regular verb ends in **-ed** (cleaned, damaged). Irregular verbs have their own forms (**done**, **built**, **taken**).

lesson.heading: Present: am/is/are + past participle
lesson.text: Use **am/is/are + past participle** for things that happen again and again, or that are true now.

lesson.heading: Past: was/were + past participle
lesson.text: Use **was/were + past participle** for things that happened in the past. For the place and date of your birth we always use **was/were born**.

examples.text: We **weren't invited** to the party last week.
*A:* **Was** anybody **injured** in the accident? *B:* Yes, two people **were taken** to hospital.

lesson.heading: passive + by ...
lesson.text: If you want to say who did the action, use **by**.

examples.text: The telephone was invented **by Alexander Bell** in 1876.
I was bitten **by a dog** a few days ago.
Do you like these paintings? They were painted **by a friend of mine**.

lesson.text: The passive always needs two parts: a form of **be** (am/is/are/was/were) *and* a past participle. One part alone is wrong.

exercises.prompt: Put the words in order to say what glass is made from.

exercises.explanation: Stamps is plural and this happens every day: are + sold.

exercises.prompt: Match each active sentence with the same idea in the passive.

pairs.left: Somebody cleans the office every day.
pairs.right: The office is cleaned every day.
The telephone was invented by Alexander Bell.

pairs.left: A dog bit me a few days ago.
pairs.right: I was bitten by a dog a few days ago.

pairs.left: A friend of mine painted these pictures.
pairs.right: These pictures were painted by a friend of mine.

exercises.prompt: You do not know how to say a new word. What do you ask?
exercises.explanation: Passive question: is + this word + pronounced.
last month is past, and one house, so: was + painted.

exercises.prompt: My phone ___ a few days ago.

exercises.explanation: Three people is plural and this is past: were + injured.
For the place of birth we say was born, never am born.

exercises.prompt: You want to know the date of this bridge. Write the question.
exercises.explanation: Past passive question: was + this bridge + built.

exercises.statement: Football plays in most countries of the world.
exercises.explanation: Football is played in most countries of the world. People play football, so football needs the passive.

exercises.statement: How many languages are speaking in Switzerland?
exercises.explanation: How many languages are spoken in Switzerland? The passive needs the past participle spoken, not speaking.
